item.title: UK allows US to use bases to strike Strait of Hormuz targets
item.summary: Downing Street said ministers approved the expansion after accusing Iran of "reckless strikes".

item.title: Iranian strikes on bases used by US caused $800m in damage, new analysis shows
item.summary: Much of the damage was caused in initial retaliatory strikes by Iran in the week after the US and Israel launched its operation.

item.title: Watch: Israeli strike next to British journalist is not AI-generated
item.summary: The video of the strike, hitting just metres from RT's Steve Sweeney and his crew, was recorded on Thursday in southern Lebanon.

item.title: Trump makes Pearl Harbor remark in meeting with Japan's PM
item.summary: President Trump compared US strikes on Iran to the deadly 1941 Japanese attack and declaration of war as part of World War Two.

item.title: 'I feel so grateful to be alive,' says Kent University meningitis survivor
item.summary: Annabelle Mackay, 21, has spoken to the BBC about her experience surviving meningitis.

item.title: Ukraine-Hungary oil pipeline row threatens EU loan
item.summary: Kyiv and Budapest disagree on how badly damaged a hub in western Ukraine bombed by Russia really is, as its oil flow remains suspended.

item.title: Sir Chris Hoy says terminal cancer diagnosis taught him how to live
item.summary: The six times Olympic cycling champion says a "bucket list" is less important than learning to appreciate special small things "in the moment".

item.title: Iranian man arrested trying to enter Faslane nuclear base
item.summary: A 34-year-old man and a 31-year-old woman were arrested at HM Naval Base Clyde, which houses UK's nuclear-armed submarines, on Thursday.

item.title: Tenerife hit by snow as Storm Therese brings wind and rain to Canary Islands
item.summary: Authorities in Tenerife have activated their emergency plans with roads closed and events cancelled as weather warnings are in force.

item.title: Work from home and drive more slowly to save energy, global body urges
item.summary: People should change how they travel, work and cook to tackle the energy price crisis, the International Energy Agency says.
